explicit_propositions.text: The speaker had a dream to save unhoused disabled mothers and young girls.
The speaker grew up in poverty with their mother, experiencing homelessness and systemic oppression.
The speaker’s mother encouraged them to pursue their dreams despite hardship.
Philanthropic institutions often appropriate grassroots movements and erase original creators.
The Ford Foundation took over the Poor People's Economic Human Rights Campaign and transformed it into a middle-class-led initiative.
Academic and nonprofit actors frequently profit from the struggles of marginalized communities without proper attribution.
The UN Rapid Tiers report excluded Hopefulness and other grassroots groups from its narrative.
Media consolidation has led to the erasure of Indigenous and poor-led journalism efforts.
Some poor and BIPOC individuals participate in systems that exploit their communities due to financial necessity.
Solidarity, mutual aid, and horizontal love are essential to building a liberated future.

assumptions.text: Authentic liberation requires leadership from those directly impacted by oppression.
Institutional power structures inherently reproduce capitalist exploitation under the guise of reform.
Historical continuity and memory are critical to maintaining integrity in social movements.
Grants and funding mechanisms are tools of control and co-optation within social justice spaces.
People engaged in survival work may unintentionally perpetuate harm due to lack of historical awareness.
Mutual recognition and shared visibility among grassroots groups strengthen collective resistance.
Indigenous sovereignty and ancestral stewardship are foundational to any genuine environmental or social justice movement.
Language, representation, and image are sites of ideological contestation and cultural appropriation.
The academic-industrial complex benefits from distancing itself from lived experience while claiming expertise.
True transformation requires dismantling hierarchies rooted in race, class, disability, and gender.
